title: AM compliance ritual — Jordan Patel
content:
Morning ritual (quick, 15–25m) - 2026-03-13

Purpose: triage the day for SOC2 evidence ingestion, vendor follow-ups, and small policy TODOs I can clear before noon. Keep this fast and actionable.

Top-of-day snapshot:
- Last upload batch: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2026-03/ (size: ~420MB) — confirm processing job finished (lambda: evidence-processor-prod) — last run 03:04 UTC.
- Incoming vendor package: LogWeave assessment packet (email from compliance@logweave.io) — PDF + spreadsheet attached.
- Outstanding access review: Okta group 'external-vendors' expires 2026-03-20 (reminder scheduled).

Immediate 15-min checklist:
1) Verify S3 batch processed and indexed (evidence-processor logs) — if ERROR, run: aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/evidence-processor-prod --start-time <yesterday> --query 'events[?message.contains(@, `ERROR`)]'  (estimate 5m) — assign to Samira if shows 5+ errors.
2) Quick glance at the LogWeave packet — check for SOC2 Type II, date, scope (does it include hosting/infra?) — note: their attestation says 'subservice' for 'infrastructure providers' only (likely insufficient). Write quick note to vendor asking for system-level scope or clarifying controls (SEC-482). (estimate 7m)
3) Okta access audit — open ticket to kick off quick review for 6 users flagged last week (JIRA: ID OKTA-77) — add Miguel as reviewer. (estimate 3m)

Notes on LogWeave (vendor review quickscan):
- Received: 2026-03-12 17:22 PST.
- Files: logweave_soc2_report_2024Q4.pdf, control-matrix.xlsx, asset-inventory.csv.
- Quick finds: report lists encryption control but references 'customer-managed keys via provider' — need explicit KMS ownership proof.
- Action: ask for evidence of KMS rotation policy and a sample audit record. Draft message: Hi — can you share KMS rotation logs and clarify whether the scope includes key custody? Also, who performed the last independent penetration test?
- Priority: medium — client-facing path depends on timeline, but vendor onboarding won't block current rollout unless we see a gap in data isolation controls.

SOC2 evidence to close this week (personal priorities):
- CC6: logging configuration for inference runtime (serving-runtime/gpu-cluster) — collect fluentd conf and sample log bundle (where: /ops/serving-runtime/logging/2026-03). Owner: Jordan (me). ETA: 2026-03-15.
- CC7: encryption at rest proof for dedicated instances — need EBS snapshot encryption metadata + KMS key ARN from infra team. Linked ticket: INFRA-129. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- CC8: external access review evidence — compile Okta export CSV and review notes. Owner: Samira. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Quick snippets to paste into Confluence later (so I don't forget):
- "Fluentd pipeline uses s3-output v2.1.3; index keys prefixed with customer-id/date; retention policy set to 90 days; logs forwarded to evidence-bucket via role redwood-evidence-uploader. Need sample of uploader role assume logs (assume-role event)."
- "For dedicated capacity, confirm that disk encryption is enabled by default and provide a snapshot ID with encryption flag set. Note which KMS key used and whether key policy allows Redwood Security team audit."

Unresolved questions (ping list):
- Does LogWeave's control matrix map to our CC criteria 6/7/8? (ping Samira)
- Who on infra can produce the EBS snapshot sample quickly? (ping Miguel)
- Are there any outstanding evidence uploads older than 7 days that didn't get processed? (check evidence-processor alerting)

Mini action plan for next hour:
- 08:45 — run evidence-processor logs check + send Samira note if errors > 5.
- 08:55 — open quick vendor clarifying email to LogWeave, include request list and 48h turnaround expectation. (use canned template in Confluence: Vendor Intake > Quick clarifying email)
- 09:10 — create Okta review JIRA (OKTA-77) and add Miguel + product-security alias.

Things to capture for SOC2 doc bundle (short checklist):
- File naming convention: SOC2_CC#_<artifact-type>_<YYYYMMDD>_<owner>.pdf (we agreed on this in last sync).
- Evidence metadata: control mapped, source system, collection method, retention, reviewer, link to raw artifact (S3 path).
- Quick tags: 'accepted', 'needs_followup', 'not_in_scope'.

If I get blocked:
- Escalate to Samira for vendor escalations (she has vendor review cadence).
- If infra is slow, open a P0 slack thread in #infra-ops and tag Miguel.

Random mental notes (for later):
- Remember to update the 'Third-party access' matrix with LogWeave once they confirm KMS approach.
- Reconcile the evidence manifest with the audit checklist we exported last month (Confluence export id: export-2026-02-11).

End-of-session log (quick):
- 09:25 — Evidence-processor: 0 errors, indexing complete. (nice)
- 09:32 — Sent vendor clarifying email (copied Samira).
- 09:40 — Created OKTA-77 and assigned Miguel + product-security.

TODO (short, prioritized):
- [P0] Collect fluentd sample bundle and upload to evidence S3 (me) — due 2026-03-15.
- [P1] Follow up with LogWeave on KMS rotation proof (Samira) — due 2026-03-15.
- [P1] Get EBS snapshot metadata from infra (Miguel) — due 2026-03-16.
- [P2] Run monthly access review exports and attach CSV to Confluence review page (me) — due 2026-03-20.

Tiny wins to aim for before lunch:
- Close one P1 (vendor question) and move P0 to 'in progress'.

Signed off — jordan

Notes-to-self: Keep this doc ephemeral; once artifacts are uploaded and tickets created, create a tidy entry in Confluence and delete this note or convert to meeting minutes.
